Name: Stardewiki
Author: Stopthatstings
Description:
Enough time for another harvest? Missing an ingredient? One more gift before the weekly limit?

[b]Stardewiki brings the wiki and your current game information together in your pause menu[/b], so you can make a plan and get back to your farm.

Read about crops, villagers, gifts, recipes, items and places without switching windows. Open the [b]Wiki tab[/b] or press [b]F1[/b], type what you're looking for, and choose a result. You don't need to own an item or have discovered it first.

[b]Green Game cards[/b] use your loaded game data and current save.

[b]Blue Wiki cards[/b] bring you the community's guides, tables and articles.

[b]Purple Modded labels[/b] identify supported content added or changed by the mods your game has loaded.

Matching labels stay visible while you read, so you always know where the information comes from.
[line]
[b][size=5]Features[/size][/b]
[list]
[*][b]Browse the wiki in-game.[/b]
Read articles, follow links, view images, and jump to sections like Gifts, Locations or Sell Prices.
[/*]
[*][b]Make the most of today.[/b]
Check weather, time, energy, health, luck, active buffs and skill XP in [b]My day[/b]. See birthday reminders, ready crops and machine output at a glance.
[/*]
[*][b]Plan your next step.[/b]
Check planting windows, missing recipe ingredients, villager relationships, animal care, building materials and more against your current game.
[/*]
[*][b]Find the ingredients you already have.[/b]
Cooking, crafting and building plans count your backpack, fridges and chests separately. See what's missing and which chest to check before gathering more.
[/*]
[*][b]Make room for longer pages.[/b]
Expand the reader for wide tables and images, then return to the menu without losing your place.
[/*]
[*][b]Save your regular lookups.[/b]
Keep favorites and recent pages handy. Articles and images you've already downloaded can be read offline.
[/*]
[*][b]Start over without losing anything.[/b]
The X beside search clears the current lookup and returns Home. Your favorites, history and saved pages stay put.
[/*]
[*][b]Use the menu you already have.[/b]
The Wiki tab works with the regular pause menu and with Better Game Menu.
[/*]
[*][b]Controller-friendly navigation.[/b]
Use a controller to move focus, select, go back, scroll, and navigate Stardewiki from the pause menu. Physical-device testing is still expanding, so controller feedback is especially welcome.[/*]
[/list][line]
[b][size=5]Modded content support[/size][/b]

Added a new crop and wondering whether there's time to grow it? Found an unfamiliar ingredient and want to know which mod it came from?

Stardewiki can look up supported content from the mods you have loaded, right alongside the rest of your game.

[b]Included in Stardewiki 0.2.0, the recommended Main File.[/b]

Modded-content support is automatic when compatible content is loaded. Stardewiki also works with vanilla Stardew Valley; no content mods or separate Stardewiki add-on are required.

The preserved [b]0.1.0-rc.1[/b] download is a legacy / rollback build from before modded-content support. Most players should use [b]0.2.0[/b]. Install only one Stardewiki version at a time.

[list]
[*][b]Look up more of your game.[/b]
Find added crops, seeds, items, fish, villagers and locations using the data your game actually loaded. Supported recipe and equipment records appear alongside them.
[/*]
[*][b]See where something came from.[/b]
[b]Purple labels[/b] distinguish added content alongside the existing green Game and blue Wiki labels. Open [b]Source[/b] for available mod names, versions, authors and attribution details. Changes to vanilla entries are identified too; uncertain or shared ownership stays qualified.
[/*]
[*][b]Focus your search.[/b]
Cycle [b]Source: All / Game / Modded[/b] to narrow the results. Prefer the base-game catalog? Turn off [b]Include modded content in search[/b] in Settings.
[/*]
[*][b]Keep useful context.[/b]
Supported custom crops get planting forecasts, ingredients keep their backpack/fridge/chest counts, and added fish use the same season, weather, time and skill checks. Special mod rules that Stardewiki can't evaluate stay uncertain.
[/*]
[*][b]Keep custom lookups local.[/b]
Recognized modded names and IDs use local game cards without an automatic Wiki request or a guess at an unrelated vanilla article.[/*]
[/list]The new screenshots show [b]Stardew Valley Expanded[/b] crops and items in a real game session.

SVE is an example, not a requirement. Support depends on how each mod supplies its data; see Compatibility below for the current limits.
[line]
[b][size=5]Information from your game[/size][/b]

The [b]Game[/b] view goes beyond the usual reference page. It reads the state of your game and updates while the card is open.
[list]
[*][b]Skills and status[/b]
Earned XP, progress to the next level, temporary skill bonuses, professions and recipe unlocks.
[/*]
[*][b]Crops and orchards[/b]
Planting outlook, first-harvest dates, seasonal regrowth windows, ready crop tiles and fruit-tree maturity. Crop estimates include Agriculturist and explain their watering and soil assumptions.
[/*]
[*][b]Cooking and crafting[/b]
Whether you've learned a recipe, ingredients across your backpack, fridges and chests, what's still missing and how many batches your materials cover. Chest locations help you find what to collect. Shared storage counts once, even when several chests open the same inventory.
[/*]
[*][b]Villagers and gifts[/b]
Friendship hearts, gifts today and this week, birthdays, current loaded positions and how a villager feels about the item you're holding.
[/*]
[*][b]Farm and workshop[/b]
Animal care meters, unpetted animals, building costs and materials, construction progress and the timers on your placed machines.
[/*]
[*][b]Exploration and collections[/b]
Current local conditions, equipment, mine progress, active quests, museum donations and other recorded collection counts. Shop cards show listed stock rules and supported player conditions.
[/*]
[*][b]Fishing[/b]
Your skill, location, season, time, weather, rod and bait, plus supported story requirements. See what's possible here and what still needs checking.[/*]
[/list]These cards use the data your game has loaded, including compatible data changes.

Open a resource's Game card to see how much is in your backpack, fridges and chests. Counts refresh while you read, so moving ingredients updates the answer.

Stardewiki helps you plan with what you have. It doesn't move items, craft remotely, give gifts or change your progress.

Having enough ingredients somewhere on the farm doesn't mean you can use them from where you're standing. Collect what you need, and let the game's crafting or cooking menu handle the rest.

Uncertain requirements stay conditional; future loot and random outcomes stay a surprise.
[line]
[b][size=5]How to use[/size][/b]

Start with [b]My day[/b], or try:
[list]
[*][b]Can I plant Ancient Fruit today?[/b][/*]
[*][b]Can I craft a Sprinkler?[/b][/*]
[*][b]How much XP for Farming?[/b][/*]
[/list]You can also look up [b]Abigail[/b], [b]Maki Roll[/b], [b]The Mines[/b] or any other wiki subject.

Choose a result, switch between [b]Wiki[/b] and [b]Game[/b] where both are available, and use the section tabs to reach the part you need.

[size=4][b]Shortcuts and navigation[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]F1[/b] opens Stardewiki.[/*]
[*][b]F2[/b] looks up the item you're holding.[/*]
[*]The button in the reader's upper-right corner expands or restores the reader.[/*]
[*][b]Escape[/b] leaves the search box first, returns an expanded reader to the menu next, and then closes the menu.[/*]
[/list]Controller users can navigate the reader with normal menu controls for focus, selection/back and scrolling. Search text entry uses the game's text-entry interface.

You can change shortcuts, switch offline mode on or off, and manage downloaded pages in [b]Settings[/b].

If another mod already uses F1, choose a different key there.
[line]
[b][size=5]Install[/size][/b]
[list=1]
[*]Install [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/2400]SMAPI[/url].
You'll need SMAPI [b]4.5.2+[/b] and Stardew Valley [b]1.6.15+[/b].
[/*]
[*]Close the game and unzip Stardewiki into your [b]Mods[/b] folder.
The folder should contain:
[b]Mods/Stardewiki/manifest.json[/b]
[/*]
[*]Start the game through SMAPI.
Look for the chicken-and-book Wiki tab at the right of your pause menu, or press [b]F1[/b].[/*]
[/list][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/32032]Better Game Menu[/url] is optional.

If the tab can't be added, you can still open the reader with the Wiki button or shortcut.

[size=4][b]Updating[/b][/size]

Replace the files from the download, but keep your [b]config.json[/b] and [b]data/[/b] folder to preserve settings and saved references.

[size=4][b]Choosing a download[/b][/size]

Download [b]Stardewiki 0.2.0[/b] from Main Files. It includes the full mod for vanilla and supported modded setups.

Install only one Stardewiki version at a time. Keep a backup of your current Stardewiki folder when updating.

SVE and Content Patcher are not required by Stardewiki itself. Install any dependencies required by the content mods you choose.

[size=4][b]Uninstalling[/b][/size]

Close the game and remove the Stardewiki folder.

Keep a copy of [b]data/[/b] if you'd like to save your favorites and downloaded pages.
[line]
[b][size=5]Offline reading and privacy[/size][/b]

New wiki searches need an internet connection.

Previously downloaded articles, images and the game's reference cards are available offline; the whole wiki isn't included in the download.

Viewed pages are checked for updates after 24 hours by default, and the reader shows when you're using a saved copy.

[b]Original[/b] opens the source article in your browser.

Online mode sends your searches and page/image requests to the official Stardew Valley Wiki.

It does [b]not[/b] send:
[list]
[*]save files[/*]
[*]installed mod lists[/*]
[*]player identifiers[/*]
[*]credentials[/*]
[*]diagnostic logs[/*]
[/list]There are no analytics.

Offline mode stops wiki requests. No account or paid API is needed, and Stardewiki doesn't download its own mod updates.

[b]Recognized custom subjects stay local[/b] unless you explicitly choose a Wiki search.

Looking up a supported modded item does not automatically send its name to the Wiki or select an unrelated vanilla article.
[line]
[b][size=5]Compatibility[/size][/b]

This is an early release for [b]Windows/Steam[/b], tested with:
[list]
[*][b]Stardew Valley 1.6.15[/b][/*]
[*][b]SMAPI 4.5.2[/b][/*]
[*][b]Better Game Menu 1.0.1[/b], both installed and absent[/*]
[/list]Other platforms, game versions and menu mods haven't been verified.

Multiplayer and split-screen also still need testing.

[size=4][b]Controller support[/b][/size]

[b]Controller navigation is supported[/b], including:
[list]
[*]focus movement[/*]
[*]selection and back[/*]
[*]scrolling[/*]
[*]opening and using the reader through the game menu[/*]
[/list]The controller input paths have been tested in development, but coverage across different physical controllers, drivers and Steam Input configurations is still growing.

If you find a controller-specific issue, please report the controller model and whether you're using Steam Input so I can try to reproduce the underlying behavior.

[size=4][b]Modded content compatibility[/b][/size]

Mod-aware compatibility was tested with:
[list]
[*][b]Stardew Valley Expanded 1.15.11[/b] built from official source[/*]
[*][b]Content Patcher 2.9.1[/b] built from official source[/*]
[*][b]Farm Type Manager 1.26.1[/b][/*]
[/list]
This doesn't guarantee every mod pack or every SVE build.

Crops/seeds, objects, fish, villager records and location records received focused checks.

Recipes, shops, equipment and other loaded records can also appear, but special behavior added by a mod may need checking in that mod's documentation.

Source labels describe the evidence available.

A matching item ID can identify a mod's namespace; patch declarations can suggest contributors. Neither guarantees which mod made every later change.

Some entries have several possible contributors or an unknown source.

Stardewiki doesn't fully interpret:
[list]
[*]custom skill systems[/*]
[*]scripted quests[/*]
[*]custom machine rules[/*]
[*]every custom spawn system[/*]
[/list]It also doesn't include separate mod Wiki sites.
[line]
[b][size=5]Known limitations[/size][/b]

[size=4][b]Wiki display[/b][/size]

The controls and wiki articles are in English; game reference names use your game's language.

Some complex wiki layouts are simplified. Use [b]Original[/b] if you need to check the website's layout.

[size=4][b]Game-aware answers[/b][/size]

Game cards explain the limits of each answer.

Crop forecasts assume daily watering, no fertilizer and no paddy-water bonus.

Shop entries don't guarantee opening hours, available stock or final prices.

Collection counts aren't a perfection score.

Loaded characters and objects may change; future schedules, loot, random stock and routes aren't predicted.

Custom conditions can require checking in the game or Wiki.

[size=4][b]Storage scanning[/b][/size]

Storage counts include:
[list]
[*]ordinary and big player chests[/*]
[*]mini-fridges[/*]
[*]home, cabin and island fridges[/*]
[*]shared Junimo storage in loaded locations[/*]
[/list]They don't include:
[list]
[*]shipping bins[/*]
[*]machine storage[/*]
[*]other players' backpacks[/*]
[*]virtual storage added by other mods[/*]
[/list]
Unloaded locations or unusually large storage scans may leave more items to check; incomplete scans are labeled.

Cooking uses only the fridges available to that kitchen.

Workbenches and storage mods may have their own rules, so the card separates materials you own from materials you carry.

[size=4][b]Fishing[/b][/size]

Casting position, water depth and other rules can still matter, so eligibility doesn't guarantee a catch.

Crab-pot catches are shown separately; exact catch odds aren't included.
[line]
[b][size=5]Feedback & bug reports[/size][/b]

Stardewiki is still being actively developed, and feedback is welcome.

If you find:
[list]
[*]a bug[/*]
[*]incorrect information[/*]
[*]a mod compatibility problem[/*]
[*]a controller issue[/*]
[*]or something that simply feels awkward to use[/*]
[/list]please [b]leave a comment on the mod page or message me directly on Nexus[/b].

I can usually try to reproduce the issue on my end even if I don't have the exact same hardware or mod setup.

[size=4][b]What to include[/b][/size]

When possible, please include:

[list]
[*]your [b]Stardewiki version[/b][/*]
[*]your [b]Stardew Valley version[/b][/*]
[*]your [b]SMAPI version[/b][/*]
[*]whether you use [b]Better Game Menu[/b][/*]
[*]your [b]UI scale[/b], if the problem is visual[/*]
[*]what you were searching for, reading or doing[/*]
[*]a few steps to reproduce the problem[/*]
[*]any relevant mod names and versions[/*]
[/list][size=4][b]For controller issues[/b][/size]

Please also include:

[list]
[*]controller make/model[/*]
[*]wired, Bluetooth or wireless adapter[/*]
[*]whether [b]Steam Input[/b] is enabled[/*]
[*]which button/input you used[/*]
[*]what you expected to happen[/*]
[*]what happened instead[/*]
[/list]
You don't need to post saves or personal information publicly.

Please mention the relevant content mod and version when the problem involves custom content.
[line]
AI was used to assist in the development of this mod and creation of the cover illustration. Gameplay screenshots are unaltered; the mod has no in-game AI service.
